schema_note: One table ("tests"), keyed by test_id, with every per-test fact nested inside its own entry - no join needed to read one test whole. To flatten into separate SQL tables later: tests (drop call_sequence/asserts/tags/displays/initial_chosen_cells/initial_blocked_cells, add test_id as a column), call_sequence (test_id, step, function_name, map_changed, raised), asserts (test_id, assert_id, assertion, evaluated_at_step, note), tags (test_id, tag), displays (test_id, display_id, position, flags.*, note) - each is already exactly that shape, just nested. initial_chosen_cells/initial_blocked_cells are [row, col] pairs; a cell absent from both is free. call_sequence.step is 1-based and numbers the exact function-call order do_closure (or the hand-orchestrated equivalent named in that test's free_text) executed - see free_text for which; call_sequence.raised is true on the one step (if any) whose call raised InvalidTilingError, which is still recorded (the exception is raised, not swallowed - see tests.raised_message). "bidirectional link" (tag has-bidirectional-link/no-bidirectional-link) is this team's term for what the codebase itself sometimes calls an "eye": two cells that directly force each other (A in B.forces and B in A.forces). displays is every representation.display_closure_step call belonging to this test's own recorded call_sequence (both do_closure's own internal call, when show=True, and any call the test makes directly around it) - "position" is the call_sequence step number after which the display occurs (0 = before any step ran); "flags" are the arguments that actually vary display to display (show_links, show_real, show_entries_terminals, margin - null or {width, crop} - and roi_margin), omitting the always-present ax/colormap/title plumbing. A display already occupying its own call_sequence entry (function_name "display_closure_step", when do_closure ran with show=True) still gets a displays entry at the same position, since call_sequence itself does not carry these flags - the two are complementary, not duplicates. Displays belonging to a different do_closure call than the one this scorecard's call_sequence recorded (an earlier or later round in the same source test, or a run on a separate copy of the map) are out of scope and omitted, with a note on the nearest in-scope display item explaining what was left out.

test_rectangle.free_text: Smallest input that gets a seat started: two vertically-stacked blocked cells at (2,3)/(3,3), nothing else. Each threatens the seat forming immediately to its own side.

displays.note: Called after do_closure completes and after the test's own redundant check_tiling_invariant(m) re-check (not itself a call_sequence entry). Title: '4: check_tiling_invariant (invariant held - no state change)'.

test_line.free_text: Six squares placed so their blocked diagonal neighbours pair into three mutual alert-blocking quadrants, chained by a plain diagonal link from (9,1). Unbranched, so get_blocked_links is empty in the original stage-by-stage test.

displays.note: Position is approximate: the ORIGINAL source test displays here after only find_alerts_set_links + assign_paths + get_blocked_links (3 calls) - it never calls find_secondary_links (this scorecard's step 2) before this display. This scorecard's call_sequence is a full do_closure reconstruction run separately on the same initial board, for parity with the other scorecards. Title: 'line (simple chain): alert_blocked=blue, alert_chosen=yellow, both=green'.

test_tree_fan_out.free_text: Four squares each alert-block one diagonal neighbour of the shared centre (4,4) via a separate corner, so (4,4) ends up forcing all four despite never being alert_chosen itself - .forces and .alert_chosen are independent facts.

asserts.assertion: each of (2,2),(2,6),(6,2),(6,6) is alert_chosen with (4,4) in forced_by

displays.note: Called after the full call_sequence completes and after a redundant get_blocked_links(m) re-check (not itself a call_sequence entry). Title: 'tree (fan-out)'.

test_tree_fan_in.free_text: (3,3) is forced_by four separate items at once - (2,1),(4,1),(4,3),(4,5) - none needing any of the others. Either of two different later placements (6,4) or (2,1)) reaches it via forced_closure, confirming it's a real fan-in, not just one link in a chain.

displays.note: Title: 'line into cycle' - the display tied to this scorecard's own recorded call_sequence (the first of the source test's three do_closure/display rounds).

Title: 'fan-in forced via (6, 4)' - occurs after an additional place_squares(forced_closure(m, (6, 4))) call made directly by the test, outside do_closure and not represented in call_sequence. A third display ('fan-in forced via (2, 1)') exists in the source test but belongs to a second, independent do_closure call on a fresh copy of the same initial grid - out of scope for this scorecard's single call_sequence, so omitted here.

test_line_into_eye.free_text: (1,4) is a pure diagonal linker into (1,6): it has real .forces without being alert_chosen itself. (1,6) and (1,8) are a genuine mutual pair - each is alert_chosen and forces the other - a real bidirectional link. Placing (1,4) afterwards (outside do_closure, via forced_closure+place_squares) drags both bidirectionally-linked cells chosen too.

asserts.assertion: m[1,4].path_id == set() (single-target entry pruned by assign_paths)

displays.note: Title: 'line into cycle: after placing (1, 4)' - occurs after an additional place_squares(forced_closure(m, (1, 4))) call, outside do_closure and not represented in call_sequence.

test_eye_outwards.free_text: A bidirectional link with a line feeding outwards from it in the opposite direction from test_line_into_eye - display-only in the source test, no assertions there, so this scorecard's asserts are left empty; useful as a pure structural example.

displays.note: Title: 'cycle line outwards: after placing (1, 2)' - occurs after an additional place_squares(forced_closure(m, (1, 2))) call, outside do_closure and not represented in call_sequence.

test_get_and_set_blocked_links_marks_blo.free_text: Border-wrapped 12x12 board with two hand-placed dominoes. Not a full do_closure call: only one round, and find_secondary_links is skipped entirely (this test predates/bypasses it), so the 5-step sequence here is a strict subsequence of do_closure's own. get_blocked_links finds six self-contradicting path ids ({26,33,62,64,90,117}); set_blocked_links blocks their six origin cells outright. Five of the six are later locally confirmed by a seat place_square_in_seat_closed fills next to them - (5,2) is the exception, with no bordering seat, invisible to any purely local read of the resulting board. This is the concrete case do_closure's own docstring cites for why get_blocked_links/set_blocked_links has to run before place_square_in_seat_closed at all.

asserts.assertion: no cell's path_id retains any id in p; no cell's forces/forced_by retains any blocked_tmp position
new seats fill 4 of the 6 corroborating positions; (5,2) has no bordering new seat

displays.note: Falls between this scorecard's step 4 (set_blocked_links) and step 5 (place_square_in_seat_closed) - blocked_tmp cells show in red. Title: 'get_blocked_links/set_blocked_links: blocked_tmp in red'. A further do_closure(show=True) call follows (after clear_all_but_state), with its own separate internal display - not represented in this scorecard's 5-step call_sequence.

test_seat_from_two_alert_blocked.free_text: Regression case for find_secondary_links. Without it, (7,5) used to end up chosen with an empty .forced_by - discovered only by place_square_in_seat_closed's raw state scan, invisible to the alert/path bookkeeping. find_secondary_links simulates (5,4) and (7,3) both chosen together (combining candidate a=(5,4) with P=(6,3)'s promised corner B=(7,3)) and finds this jointly completes a fresh seat at (7,5) - so (5,4) gets linked to it directly, and forced_closure(m,(5,4)) now reaches (7,5) too.

displays.note: This is do_closure's own internal display (do_closure(m, 'initial', show=True)) - it already appears as the step-7 'display_closure_step' entry in call_sequence; this item adds the flags that entry doesn't carry. A further place_and_chase(...) round follows, with its own separate do_closure(show=False) call plus an external display_closure_step call - not represented here.

test_frozen_area.free_text: Same phenomenon as test_seat_from_two_alert_blocked, one round later: by the end of round 2, find_secondary_links has already linked both (6,7) and (6,8) - the two cells round 3 is about to place - directly to (8,7), so forced_closure(m,(6,7)) reaches it too, instead of leaving it for place_square_in_seat_closed's raw scan to discover once round 3's placement happens to complete its seat. Initial map here is the board state after rounds 1-2 (placing (4,4) then (5,4) and chasing each), immediately before round 3 places (6,7) and its forced_closure and this scorecard's do_closure call runs.

asserts.note: evaluated before this call sequence, on the round-2 board

displays.note: Called by place_and_chase directly, after its own internal do_closure(show=False) call (matching this scorecard's own do_closure_sequence(show=False)) - not via do_closure's own show=True branch.

test_show_other_full_2x2.free_text: Four squares placed so that closure's own placement decisions (not the hand-chosen squares directly) complete a fully-blocked 2x2 block somewhere on the board. check_tiling_invariant, run once at the very end of do_closure, catches this and raises - the whole call sequence up to and including the final check_tiling_invariant step still ran; the raise happens on that last step, not earlier.

displays.note: Title: 'initial state' - shows the four hand-placed squares before do_closure runs at all (position 0 = before any call_sequence step).
Runs even though step 14 (check_tiling_invariant) raised - the test's try/except catches InvalidTilingError and displays the resulting (invalid) board, with the error folded into the title.

test_margin_free_3x3realmap.free_text: n=2: a 3x3 free core (odd interior) wrapped in build_margin_free_map's blocked ring. do_closure's own initial closure pass raises InvalidTilingError before any square is ever placed by the caller - too small a free core cannot be validly tiled at all.

asserts.assertion: do_closure raises InvalidTilingError on its first call

displays.note: Only reached because do_closure raised InvalidTilingError at step 14 - the test's except block displays the rejected board, using the module-level MARGIN=RealSpaceMargin(width=2) and ROI_MARGIN=1.

test_margin_free_4x4realmap.free_text: n=3: a 4x4 free core wrapped in a blocked margin. The source test repeatedly picks a random still-free cell, chases its forced_closure, resets bookkeeping, and re-runs do_closure(show=True) until is_realmap_cover_complete says the real-space map has no gap left (source test does not seed random.choice, so its exact placement order varies run to run; this scorecard fixes random.seed(7) so the recorded call sequence is reproducible). initial_map here is the board state immediately before the FINAL do_closure call. Empirically (checked across dozens of seeds, both n=3 and n=5 cores), coverage always flips to complete at the manual forced_closure placement itself, one step before do_closure even runs - every field in this scorecard's map_changed_flags is false because the board is already at a local fixed point (no new alerts, no contradictions, no seats) by the time do_closure starts. do_closure's role in this final round is pure post-hoc validation - contradiction check plus check_tiling_invariant - not placement. That's a real, load-bearing fact about this pipeline, not an artifact of this particular seed.

displays.note: do_closure's own internal display (do_closure(..., show=True, margin=MARGIN, roi_margin=ROI_MARGIN)) for this final round - already appears as the step-7 'display_closure_step' entry in call_sequence; this item adds its flags.
